This file documents the sandboxes resource at the shell, one section per command. Every command is a subcommand of =sandboxes=, and every section exports its own script into =projects/ores.shell/scripts/library/=. Loading a script runs that one command, so a failure names the command it came from.

* Commands

** =list=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: FCAB5EB0-63A9-58EC-9F22-F2EFA5DB77CD
:END:

Reads one page of the collection. Nothing addresses it but the caller's tenant, so it is the read that shows what exists.


The command is shaped like this:

#+begin_example
sandboxes list [--offset <n>] [--limit <n>] [--order <field>] [--desc]
#+end_example

It is addressed at =refdata.v1.sandboxes.list=.

#+name: sandboxes-list
#+begin_src ores-shell :tangle sandboxes-list.ores :exports none

#+end_src

** =get=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: D0C8C8C4-0A3F-540F-BF45-D5F557806BB4

Reads the one row its key addresses. A key states every identifying column, so a partial key is refused rather than answered with an arbitrary row.

** =add=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: 7A2485CC-9507-512E-9909-F42A3369A230
:END:

Writes a row. The change states that the row must not exist, so a create that collides with an existing row is refused rather than replacing it. The change carries a reason and a commentary, which the server records on it so the row's history says why it moved.


The command is shaped like this:

#+begin_example
sandboxes add <name> <purpose> <anchor_portfolio_id> <owner_account_id> <visibility> <status> <review_date> <description> <reason> <commentary>
#+end_example

** =set=
:PROPERTIES:
:ID: 47AAE29E-AB2B-5C59-A1BD-61C1E1FFAFA4
:END:

Writes a row. The change states no precondition, so it replaces whatever row the key already addresses. The change carries a reason and a commentary, which the server records on it so the row's history says why it moved. Passing --version makes the write conditional on the version the caller last read.
